messages.subject: Categorical mediation model
parts:
Hi everyone,

I am running a mediation analysis with a continuous predictor (SCDiff7), a continuous outcome (SA10) and a categorical/ordered mediator (VictimSev.f)

The categorical mediator ranges from 0-2 marking victimisation severity (none, moderate, severe). 

This is my code:

FD.complete$VictimSev.f <- factor(FD.complete$VictimSev)
FD.complete["VictimSev.f"] <- lapply(FD.complete["VictimSev.f"], ordered)

MedModel1 <-'
# model

SA10 ~ c*SCDiff7 + b*VictimSev.f
VictimSev.f ~ a*SCDiff7

# Indirect effect
ab := a*b

# Total effect
Total := c + (a*b)
'
FitModel1 <- sem(MedModel1, data = FD.complete)
summary(FitModel1, fit.measures = T, standardized = T) 


I am currently having no troubles with running the code, I was just wondering whether my code is actually correct when using a categorical mediator?

If so, how would I interpret the results from this analysis. The results suggest that there is no mediation of VictimSev, however, I just want to check that the analysis is correct before I continue any further.

























Thank you for your help!

Hannah

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Categorical mediation model
parts:
The "ordered" class should apply to the vector, not to individual observations in the vector, so don't use lapply on it.

FD.complete$VictimSev.f <- ordered(FD.complete$VictimSev, levels = 0:2, 
                                   labels = c("none","moderate","severe"))

I'm not sure how lavaan treats (ordered) factors as predictors, but I would guess it just uses the underlying integers and treats it the way it would a fixed predictor.  So I think your "b" effect is estimated on the assumption of a linear effect of the mediator on the outcome.  In other words, your model assumes the same amount of mean-difference in the outcome between groups 0 and 1 as there is between groups 1 and 2.  Is that a reasonable assumption?  Maybe check your group means... I'm not really sure how to get around that in lavaan -- you can't create dummy codes for the mediator to use as a predictor, since it has to be coded as an ordinal outcome in the same model.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
